uncited: This method is a core component of adaptive density control in 3D Gaussian Splatting, where it complements opacity and loss-based pruning to remove unstable or low-contribution primitives [Parent].
The method operates by constructing a visibility mask for all scene elements across all training views and pruning those that fail to meet a minimum visibility threshold.

Convert $p_i$ to homogeneous coordinates $\tilde{p} = [x_i, y_i, z_i, 1]^T$.
Transform to Camera Coordinate System (CCS): $\tilde{p}_c = d_j \tilde{p}$.
Compute homogeneous image coordinates: $\tilde{x}_c = K \tilde{p}_c$.
Normalize by depth $z_c$ (the third component of $\tilde{p}_c$) to obtain 2D pixel coordinates: $(u, v) = \pi(p_i) = (\tilde{x}_c[0]/\tilde{x}_c[2], \tilde{x}_c[1]/\tilde{x}_c[2])$.
Check if $(u, v)$ is within the image bounds.
If not, mark $p_i$ as invisible for view $j$ ($O_{ij} = 0$) and continue to next element.
Sort elements in $M_{uv}$ by their $z$-value in the Camera Coordinate System (ascending, i.e., closest to camera first).
Mark the $\tau$ elements with the smallest $z$-values as visible.
Mark all remaining elements in $M_{uv}$ as occluded (invisible) for view $j$.
**Accumulate Gradients:** During the backward pass, accumulate the screen-space gradient magnitude for each surfel across all views.
**Check Gradient:** Identify surfels whose cumulative screen-space gradient magnitude is zero.
**Prune:** Remove surfels with zero cumulative gradient.

View-frequency is the probability that an anchor is selected in training views, correlating with the received gradient.
Anchors with view-frequency below a threshold $\tau_v$ are removed.
